sources.entry: GitProxy - Proxy for Git that applies rules and workflows to all outgoing git push operations and ensures they are compliant. It supports both HTTP/HTTPS and SSH protocols with security scanning and validation. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Nodejs/Docker

summary.one_liner: GitProxy is a FINOS application that sits between developers and a Git remote and applies configurable rules and workflows (plugins) to outgoing git push operations over HTTP/HTTPS and SSH.
summary.what_it_does: GitProxy intercepts git push operations headed to a remote such as github.com and runs them through a chain of checks before forwarding them. The README describes a security processor chain that includes secret detection via gitleaks, commit message and author validation, hidden commit detection, and pre-receive hooks. Pushes that fail checks are blocked, and the README says pushes can be approved manually or automatically through workflows. It supports both HTTP/HTTPS (basic auth and JWT tokens) and SSH (key-based auth with agent forwarding), and states that both protocols get the same scanning. It also provides audit logging. The stated goal is to let teams keep the standard branch-and-merge git workflow while meeting compliance requirements, for example in regulated financial services. It can also run locally to enforce a single developer's practices.
use_cases: enforce push policies on git pushes
scan outgoing commits for secrets before pushing
compliance checks for git workflows in regulated industries
validate commit messages and author identity before push
local pre-push guardrails for a single developer
audit logging of git push activity
how_to_run: git remote add proxy <GitProxy URL> (HTTPS) or ssh://git@localhost:2222/github.com/<user>/<repo>.git (SSH)
git config core.sshCommand "ssh -A" (SSH only, agent forwarding)
Add the repository URL to proxy.config.json so pushes are allowed; default config blocks pushes
notable: Same security processor chain for both HTTP/HTTPS and SSH pushes
Rules and workflows implemented as configurable plugins
Default configuration blocks pushes until the repository is added to proxy.config.json
Can run locally for individual developers or as a shared control point for teams
Part of the FINOS open source foundation
caveats: Default config blocks all pushes until the target repository is added to proxy.config.json
SSH use requires agent forwarding and extra setup described in docs/SSH_SETUP.md
Requires Node.js to run via npx
